A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UPipe work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original throughput, memory, runtime, and head-chunk-size experiments using Llama 3-8B and Qwen3-32B.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, supplemented by activation-management and batch-size experiments in Section 6 and C4 training-loss measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core headwise chunking and GQA scheduling algorithms remain unchanged. Section 6 adds optional procedural variants: strided activation offloading skips every Kth layer, while selective checkpointing retains attention outputs to avoid recomputation. The expanded buffer accounting does not establish a redesign of the original algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds C4 training to evaluate loss convergence, extending v1's systems-performance evaluation to training behavior on a named dataset. The original model families and long-context coverage remain.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain native PyTorch Ring Attention, USP Ring/Ulysses, and FPDT. New Table 5 additionally evaluates Ulysses with selective activation checkpointing against UPipe variants. Newly documenting FPDT's SwiGLU patch does not establish that the retained baseline experiments changed.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce substantial evaluation protocols: fixed 3M-token batches with offloading stride K=7, selective checkpointing comparisons, and a batch-size sweep from 1 to 10 with CPU activation offloading disabled. Appendix D adds 1000 C4 training steps at 128K context, batch size 1, and learning rate 10^-5, recording loss every 100 steps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained head-chunk-size ablation, Section 6 tests whether saved memory improves throughput through strided offloading, selective checkpointing, or larger batches. Appendix D adds a training-convergence check addressing numerical effects of head reordering. These substantially expand the questions experimentally investigated.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly cautions that the retained single-step runtime measurements have greater variance than the throughput measurements, especially at shorter contexts. This is a limited qualitative uncertainty disclosure; neither version reports run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or numerical variability estimates.

E6.justification: New Tables 4–6 and 10 add activation-policy, batch-size, and convergence results. For example, selective checkpointing raises UPipe throughput from 850.97 to 1056.77 tokens/second at 512K, and both methods reach loss 4.47 at step 1000. Figure 2 also revises memory values, including ALST attention memory from 37.5 to 33.0 GiB. The retained throughput, memory, and runtime tables have identical numerical entries.

T1.justification: The GQA memory factor is corrected, and Tables 2 and 7 substantively revise forward/backward accounting beyond changing units. For example, UPipe's normalized forward input-exchange term changes from 2+(gamma+1)/nu to 2+gamma/nu. New Appendix A derives buffer lifetimes, storage reuse, gradient accumulation, and stage-dependent backward peaks that v1 only tabulated.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: headwise chunking with GQA scheduling reduces attention memory while preserving throughput, with up to 87.5% intermediate-memory savings and Llama 3-8B contexts of 5M tokens on eight H100s and 8M on sixteen.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly explains when reduced CPU transfers or recomputation can convert memory savings into speed. Appendix D discusses floating-point differences from head reordering, while Appendix E explicitly discusses broader Transformer applicability and possible communication overlap. The original interpretation of long-context memory benefits remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands implementation-level documentation of buffer allocation, aliasing, release, and backward accumulation. Additional disclosures cover the custom PyTorch operator supporting selective checkpointing, new experiment parameters, FSDP2, the CPU model, and FPDT's SwiGLU patch. The code link changes from the Together account to the author's account; these disclosures do not establish reruns of retained benchmarks.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to LoongTrain, GLU Variants Improve Transformer, and the T5/C4 work, and removes the original PyTorch FSDP reference. It refines the communication-latency explanation and strengthens the stated relationship between its modified USP baseline and ALST, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens background, setup, and conclusion prose, adds an attention/GQA primer, consolidates implementation explanations, and reorganizes the appendices. Terminology and publication information are updated. The existing narrative and most methodological exposition remain recognizable; the scientific additions account for much of the expansion.

P2.justification: Four new empirical tables present the activation-policy, batch-size, and convergence studies. Existing theoretical tables use explicit normalized units, memory/runtime tables receive clearer column structures and highlighting, and figures are repositioned with revised captions and styling. This substantially expands the displayed evidence while retaining the original diagrams and benchmark plots.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation and explanation gaps: Appendix D supplies a previously absent training-convergence check, Section 6 tests practical uses of saved memory, and Appendix A derives substantially revised memory accounting. These additions strengthen confidence in the method and make its memory claims more auditable without replacing the original benchmark evidence. The convergence check remains limited to one model/dataset, and statistical uncertainty remains unquantified.
